head: 666f197ee1be38edc4d28a8b94212fc49de4be55
summary:
The code matches the design. RigLock.MachineName is renamed to SessionName at SmbRig.cs:176 and the string is byte-identical (`Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig`). The only consumer is the LoopbackShare constructor (SmbRig.cs:51). No `MachineName` identifier is left in code; the one remaining mention is the historical sentence at SL-020-scanner.md:243. The three stale comments are corrected in plain ASCII. WindowCases.ps1 still has no BOM and 0 non-ASCII bytes, and its diff is the one comment line. The doc now says plainly that runs from different sign-in sessions are not serialised, and gives the trigger for Global\.

What I ran:
- Targeted tests (SmbRigTests, WindowScriptParseTests, RigLockScopeWordingTests, RuleCopiesAgreeTests, ArchitectureRulesTests): 33/33 passed.
- Full default suite: 373/373 passed.
- StallRig, built outside FsAnalyser.slnx from its csproj (which compiles SmbRig.cs by link): 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- Fitness on the tree: all 59 rules hold.
- A temporary mutation that put back all three old comments, restored afterwards with `git checkout`: Fitness then reported 4 violations. They were StallRig/Program.cs:13, StalledShareTests.cs:17 and WindowCases.ps1:1333, the last matched by both patterns. So the builder's `including_comments: true` fix is live.

Every departure that matters was declared. One minor test-coverage finding:
- WindowScriptParseTests' summary says it catches a non-ASCII dash or quote in an edited comment.
- I measured that Windows PowerShell 5.1's ParseFile accepts such a comment with 0 errors. Only inside a string does it give errors (2).
- So for this slice's comment-only edit the test could not have failed. The file's own stated invariant, that it must be pure ASCII (WindowCases.ps1:956), has no guard.

The deferred case C-005 (cross-session exclusion) is still right to defer: Local\ is unchanged and there is no Global\ anywhere. O-006 is still owed to a person.

There is no loop: build-slice ran once, with no caused_by.

Second round: Round two found nothing new. The first round's m1 still stands.

I re-walked every reader, matcher and error path this diff adds, trying to break each one:

- **WindowScriptParseTests, error path.** If ParseFile could not read the file, would the test still pass? I ran its exact `-Command` string against a missing path under both hosts. powershell.exe 5.1.26100.9444 and pwsh 7.6.6 each still print the edition line, then report `0:0: The file could not be read`, and exit 1. So a moved, renamed or unreadable WindowCases.ps1 fails the test and does not pass silently.
- **Quoting.** The path is inside single quotes with `'` doubled, so `$`, spaces and apostrophes in the repo path are safe. The command holds no double quotes that ArgumentList quoting could mangle.
- **RigLockScopeWordingTests, file types.** The file types actually present under tests/, docs/ and eng/ (outside bin and obj) are `.cs`, `.csproj`, `.ps1`, `.md`, `.json` and `.py`. The test's TextFiles list covers every one, so no text file is skipped today.
- **Directory traversal.** There are no reparse-point directories under tests/, docs/ or eng/, so the enumeration cannot loop or leave the tree. The `/bin/` and `/obj/` exclusions work on the `/`-normalised relative path at any depth.
- **Line splitting.** File.ReadLines splits on CRLF, LF and a lone CR, and the regex's `.` crosses only non-`\n` characters. So the other line breaks can only add matches, never hide one.
- **Fitness patterns.** The `(?mi)` entries use `[^\n]*`, which spans the `\r` of a CRLF line but not the line break. The round-one mutation had already confirmed that all three SL-059 rules fire on the old wording, `///` doc comments included.

Two gaps are heuristic limits of a wording tripwire rather than defects, so I did not file them. A claim hard-wrapped across two lines evades both the test and the Fitness rules; the SL-020-scanner.md lines 242-243 wrap 'on this / machine' in historical text. The StallRig and StalledShareTests Fitness entries also match `on this machine` case-sensitively, as the design wrote them. The xUnit test is case-insensitive and covers both files.

findings.claim: WindowScriptParseTests' summary says it catches 'a dropped BOM or a non-ASCII dash or quote in an edited comment', which can 'break 5.1 where 7 still reads the file'. It cannot catch the comment case. I wrote a UTF-8 no-BOM script whose comment holds an em dash and curly quotes, and powershell.exe 5.1.26100.9444 ParseFile returned errors=0. The same characters inside a double-quoted string returned errors=2. SL-059 edits only comments, so this Theory could not have failed on the edit it was added for; it only proves the file still parses, which a comment edit cannot change. The invariant the file actually states, 'The file must be pure ASCII, read the same by Windows PowerShell 5.1 and pwsh' (WindowCases.ps1:956), has no test. The builder checked it once by command (0 non-ASCII bytes, which I re-measured), and nothing in the suite keeps it.
findings.evidence: tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs:5-12 (the claim) and :28-33 (ParseFile only). tests/window/WindowCases.ps1:956 (the ASCII invariant). Measured: temp comment.ps1 gave errors=0 and string.ps1 gave errors=2 under 5.1.
findings.fix: In WindowCases.ps1's test, add an assertion that the file has no byte >= 0x80 and no UTF-8 BOM, e.g. `Assert.DoesNotContain(File.ReadAllBytes(script), b => b >= 0x80)`, naming the offset on failure. Change the summary to say the parse check covers string literals and the byte check covers comments.

obligations.evidence: tests/window/StallRig/StallRig.csproj:17 compiles ../../FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs by link, so the rename is compiled there. I re-ran `eng/dotnet.ps1 build tests/window/StallRig/StallRig.csproj -c Release -o %TEMP%\sl059-review-stallrig`: Build succeeded, 0 warnings, 0 errors, outside FsAnalyser.slnx. The scratch output was deleted. Grep finds no `MachineName` identifier anywhere in tests/.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/WindowScriptParseTests.cs: the Theory runs powershell.exe and asserts the Desktop edition, and runs pwsh.exe and asserts Core. Each ParseFiles the edited WindowCases.ps1, and I ran both green. WindowCases.ps1 has no BOM and 0 non-ASCII bytes (measured), and its diff is one comment line. The test is weaker than its docstring; see m1.

tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/RigLockScopeWordingTests.cs:27-35 feeds in the three SL-038 stale lines (must match) and four unrelated hits (must not match), and I checked that each literal is the real line: eng/dotnet.ps1:5, .gitignore:1, WindowCases.ps1:1985 and :2118. Lines 42-61 then scan every text file under tests/, docs/ and eng/, including the real eng/dotnet.ps1. It passes. My own case-insensitive grep for machine-wide, on this machine, this machine's and MachineName outside .taad turned up only the hits the builder listed and left alone (SMB-mapping scope, SDK bootstrap, measurements, Developer Mode). None of them is about RigLock.

SmbRigTests is 18/18 green in my run: ASecondRunWaitsForTheFirst, ALiveHolderFailsTheNextRunLoudlyAndAKilledOneDoesNotBlockIt and 16 OnlyTheRigsOwnMappingsAreSwept cases. The diff to SmbRig.cs is the two identifier lines only (51 and 176). RigLock.Take (184-203) is unchanged. The full suite is 373/373.

The diff at tests/FsAnalyser.Core.Tests/Rig/SmbRig.cs:176 changes only the identifier. The literal `@"Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig"` is byte-identical on both sides, so the kernel object cannot have changed. The only reference is LoopbackShare's constructor (SmbRig.cs:51). tests/window has no string reference to FsAnalyser-SmbRig, and StallRig compiles the same SmbRig.cs by link. I did not re-run the builder's live StallRig contention test: if the lock were not held it would go on to change the machine's SMB mappings, which is a person-run opt-in. The builder's recorded run agrees with the diff.

Not measurable from here. Showing that SMB mappings are per logon session needs a second sign-in session, and spike 1 showed this agent's sandbox refuses Register-ScheduledTask. The builder says it was not done, and nothing in the tree measures it. It stays owed to validate-slice, where a person has to run it. The new doc text (SL-020-scanner.md:255-262) claims only the lock's per-session scope, which is true either way.

cases.evidence: No default-suite test builds StallRig; this shape is exercised by the build command. StallRig.csproj:17 links SmbRig.cs, and my build outside the .slnx succeeded (0/0). The builder's mutation adding `RigLock.MachineName` to Program.cs failed with CS0117. The shape, a reference compiled only outside the .slnx, is fed in.

WindowScriptParseTests.WindowCasesParses("powershell.exe","Desktop") ParseFiles the edited tests/window/WindowCases.ps1 under 5.1 and asserts the edition string, so it cannot pass on the wrong host. The shape, the edited file under 5.1, is fed in. But a comment-only edit cannot break a 5.1 parse (I measured 0 errors with an em dash and curly quotes in a comment), so the case's stated risk is only half guarded (m1).

RigLockScopeWordingTests.NothingSaysTheRigLockSpansTheMachine feeds in the unrelated shape literally: Assert.DoesNotMatch on eng/dotnet.ps1:5's 'A machine-wide 10.0.x SDK' line, .gitignore:1, and WindowCases.ps1:1985 and :2118, each verbatim from the tree. It also scans the real eng/dotnet.ps1 and WindowCases.ps1 with zero hits allowed. A pattern widened to catch the SDK line would fail it.

SmbRigTests.cs: all 18 pass in my run. They take locks by UniqueName() (SmbRigTests.cs:137, `Local\FsAnalyser-SmbRig-test-{guid}`), not SessionName, so they prove RigLock.Take's behaviour is unchanged, which is what the case asks. The constant's own value is proved by the diff, not by these tests.

Deferred (material:false), and the reason still holds against the tree. SmbRig.cs:176 is still `Local\`, no `Global\` name exists anywhere, and spike 1 recorded that the agent sandbox refuses Register-ScheduledTask, the only unattended route to a second session. No test feeds two sessions, and none could here. The trigger for doing it by hand is written at SL-020-scanner.md:258-262.

drift: The design's component 'SL-020 scanner doc scope statement' gives lives_at `docs/SL-020-scanner.md`, which does not exist. The builder correctly edited `docs/design/SL-020-scanner.md` and did not say the design's path was wrong.

The WindowCases.ps1 settled entry in .taad/fitness.yaml (the two `(?mi)` patterns) and RigLockScopeWordingTests.Claim (RigLockScopeWordingTests.cs:16-18) are the same regex written twice: `[^\n]*` in one, `.*` over single lines in the other. The fitness.yaml header (lines 15-17) says settled entries have no xUnit twin and are changed 'here only'. This one now has a wider de-facto twin that eng/rules-parity.ps1 does not compare, so widening or narrowing the pattern means editing both by hand.

The default `dotnet test` suite now needs pwsh.exe (PowerShell 7) on PATH: WindowScriptParseTests InlineData("pwsh.exe", "Core"). Before this, the only PowerShell a default-suite test launched was powershell.exe (RuleCopiesAgreeTests, SmbRig's PowerShell helper). The engine's own build goes through pwsh eng/dotnet.ps1, so this holds here, but the dependency is new and not declared.

The design's reason for C-002 ('a non-ASCII dash/quote in the new text can silently break 5.1 parsing') holds only for string literals. Measured: 5.1 ParseFile accepts non-ASCII in a comment with 0 errors. For a comment-only slice, the design's check (3) was satisfied before the edit was made.
unreviewed: .taad/slices/SL-059/*.json (design-slice-1, critique-1, critique-review-1, build-slice-1, index.json): slice records, not code. I read only index.json, as the brief directed, and took the design from the brief.
